note: Fixed prompt set. Every target in bench/ sends exactly these, in this order, so throughput and latency numbers compare. Changing this file invalidates comparisons against results produced with an earlier version; bump 'version' and keep the old file if that happens.
design: Twelve prompts, matching the 12-way concurrency the repo already documents (scripts/loadtest.py:94).

Each asks for an explanation rather than a fact, so the model generates to max_tokens instead of stopping early. A prompt answered in nine tokens makes a throughput benchmark measure prompt processing, not generation.
Roughly even prompt lengths, so no single request dominates the prefill cost.
Deliberately generic subject matter: this measures serving, not the World Cup eval set in pipeline/eval/, which is held out from everything and must never be used here.
prompts: Explain how a graphics processor differs from a central processor, and why that difference matters for running large neural networks.
Describe what happens inside a transformer model when it processes a sentence, step by step, in plain language.
Explain the difference between training a model and running inference on one, and why the hardware needs differ.
Describe why language models have a context window, what happens when a conversation exceeds it, and how systems handle that.
Explain what quantisation means for a neural network, what is gained, and what is given up.
Describe how a web server handles many simultaneous requests, and where the bottlenecks usually appear.
Explain why caching is difficult in distributed systems, with attention to invalidation.
Describe the practical differences between a relational database and a document database, and when each fits.
Explain what a container is, how it differs from a virtual machine, and why that distinction matters in production.
Describe how public key cryptography lets two strangers communicate securely over an untrusted network.
Explain what causes latency in a networked application and which parts an engineer can actually control.
Describe how version control systems track changes, and why branching and merging are harder than they first appear.
